deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 1983-84 Grothendieck studied the combinatorial and topological 'space' of configurations of pseudo-lines. Its vertices are generic positions. Its edges are elementary moves, such as passing a line through a crossing. Its 2-cells should come from loops ('circuits') around codimension-2 degenerate positions; here these are the 'positions superposi-singulières'. The previous page sets up dihedral bookkeeping: involutions sigma_0..sigma_{N-1} with sigma_N = sigma_0, and rho_i = sigma_{i-1} sigma_i, the rotations of an N-gon.

This page treats one local model, the case '(-infinity, b)' of extending the banks ('rives') of a band. The figures show two pseudo-lines D (yellow) and D' (green). Each carries a pencil of transversal strands (F, yellow; F', green). They are drawn superposed along a common segment (dashed), which two red lines cross in an X at one point.

To build a 2-dimensional cell space one must glue the half-disc/band pieces attached to D and D' (the faces Delta*_D and Delta*_{D'}) along an identification a ~ b of their edges. Two choices are compared.

(1) Gluing by parallel transport.
- One obtains a space script-X with a map phi: script-X -> X that is an immersion.
- script-X carries a topological graph K. The faces of (script-X, K) correspond to the stable p.v. (stable positions).
- L = phi^{-1}(X_1), the preimage of the 1-skeleton or singular locus, realises the correspondence between faces and stable positions. To make it exact, each face F is replaced by an 'inflated' face F~, swollen at the points of K ∩ S(L) that are 'contiguous' to the singular set.
- NB (a monodromy computation): start from an orientation omega_F of F = Delta*_D, hence an orientation omega_D of D. Transport it through the gluing to Delta*_{D'}, hence get omega_{D'}. This is the opposite of the orientation of D' given by parallel transport.
- Marginal note: the trouble is that one then does not get the correct circuits around superposed-singular positions.

(2) Gluing by the isomorphism a ~ b opposite to parallel transport.
- Now the transition omega_F -> omega_{F'}, read as omega_D -> omega_{D'}, agrees with parallel transport.
- Contrary to his expectation, the correct circuits around the superposed-singular positions do appear.

The next page notes that more general circuits remain mysterious. It then tries to obtain both gluings at once by assembling two rectangles glued along two pairs of edges into a Möbius band.

In modern terms, this is an orientation-twisted (local-system / orientation double cover) phenomenon in building a cellular 2-complex whose 2-cells are the polygons bounded by flip-circuits around codimension-2 strata. The sign twist is the familiar one-sidedness of a pseudo-line in RP^2: its tubular neighbourhood is a Möbius band.
errors: No outright error. The statement that phi is an immersion and the face/stable-position correspondence (after 'inflating' faces) are asserted without proof.

The text itself flags that choice (1) yields the wrong circuits. The real issue is that the correct gluing is orientation-reversing relative to parallel transport, which is consistent with the Möbius-band (projective) nature of pseudo-line neighbourhoods. The page records this as an empirical discovery rather than explaining it.
The general circuits are left open (next page: 'restent mystérieux').

ideas.what: Building a 2-dimensional cell complex of pseudo-line configurations: vertices are generic positions, edges are elementary moves, 2-cells are circuits around codimension-2 ('superposed-singular') degenerations.
ideas.modern_name: Flip/mutation 2-complex of pseudoline arrangements; higher Bruhat order B(n,2) and its cellular realisations; discriminantal arrangements

ideas.what: Choice of gluing map between face-discs (parallel transport vs. its opposite) detected by an orientation-monodromy computation. Only the orientation-reversing gluing gives the correct circuits.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation local system / twisted gluing; Möbius-band neighbourhood of a pseudo-line in RP^2

ideas.what: Replacing faces by 'inflated' faces F~ at points of K ∩ S(L) so that faces correspond bijectively to stable positions.
ideas.modern_name: Cellular resolution / real blow-up of singular points in a stratified space

ideas.what: Dihedral reflection/rotation bookkeeping, rho_i = sigma_{i-1} sigma_i (previous page), for the polygon around a codimension-2 stratum.
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral group presentation; polygon relations in Coxeter/Artin-type presentations

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck was trying to build a cellular 2-complex of pseudo-line configurations whose 2-cells are circuits around codimension-2 degenerations. This anticipates in spirit the Manin–Schechtman higher Bruhat orders and the cellular models of discriminantal arrangements (1989 onward). He also adds an orientation-twist (Möbius-band) subtlety in the gluing, which those works handle differently, in the oriented/affine setting.
missed.quote: Contrairement à ce que je [croyais] on trouve les bons circuits autour des positions superposi-singulières
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context only. The projective (non-orientable) version of flip complexes, with its sign twist, is less standard than the affine/oriented higher Bruhat theory, but the page gives no finished result.

missed.claim: The status of the 'more general circuits' (whether all 2-cells/relations are generated by the superposed-singular ones) is left open.
missed.quote: Mais les circuits plus généraux restent mystérieux pour moi (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This corresponds to the question of the simple connectivity / presentation of the flip graph of projective pseudoline arrangements. That question is largely answered in the affine case (Ringel's theorem, higher Bruhat orders); the page adds nothing beyond posing it.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page of exploratory topology inside Grothendieck's little-known pseudo-line project. It contains a sign/orientation observation about gluings and a local model, both essentially routine. Its only interest is as an early, independent attempt at a flip 2-complex of pseudoline arrangements, with no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: 'qui matérialise la cour. [?]' should read 'qui matérialise la corr[espondance]' (between faces and stable p.v.).

The margin note reads approximately: 'L'ennui, c'est que les circuits sont irréductibles(?). On n'obtient pas les bons circuits superposi-singuliers!' The machine reading 'On n'obtient que par les pour circuits superposi-singuliers' is garbled.
The left-margin note beside 'NB Ici' seems to mention D ∩ Delta*_D and D' ∩ Delta*_{D'} (prolongation), not '$D \neq \Delta_D^*$'. It is uncertain.
'Cas (-∞, b)' is followed by a struck-out phrase, then 'de prolongation des rives' (underlined).
